name: NPRK "Mul"

placement_rationale.text: Mul's job is running the last, most exposed mile of resupply and casualty evacuation directly into the trench line, not staging from a rear depot — its representative position has to sit at the same close-in depth (doctrine.md's 1-5km close-reconnaissance band) as the positions it serves, since the entire point is replacing a human carrying party on that specific short, watched run. A deeper siting would misrepresent what the platform actually does.

image.caption: No open-licensed photograph found for this specific system — showing its category symbol.

cost.display: Domestic production, unit cost not publicly disclosed

characteristics: Strength: Highest load capacity among the smaller Ukrainian UGVs catalogued here, useful for resupply and casualty evacuation over the last dangerous kilometers
Limitation: Manual remote control (not autonomous) requires an operator in continuous contact, which is itself an EW-vulnerable link
Estimated quantity available: Fielded numbers not publicly disclosed
employment_notes: Directly reduces the need for soldiers to carry heavy loads (ammunition, water) or expose themselves during casualty evacuation across the most exposed final stretch to a position
contrast_vs_traditional: Traditional resupply doctrine sent a manned vehicle or a soldier on foot across exactly the kind of open, watched ground doctrine.md identifies as the most dangerous terrain on this front. An unmanned logistics and casualty-evacuation platform removes a person from that specific exposure without changing what has to physically move — supplies forward, wounded back.

notes: Written from doctrine.md and general knowledge; no per-asset citation yet.
